task_description: Write a method in Dafny that takes in an array and an integer L and splits the given array into two parts where the length of the first part of the array is L, and returns the resulting array in a sequence.
specification_response:
Method Signature:
    method SplitArrayAtL(a: array<int>, L: int) returns (result: seq<int>)
Postconditions_prompt:
    - The resulting sequence contains all elements of the input array in order
- The length of the sequence is equal to the length of the input array
- The first L elements of the sequence correspond to the first L elements of the input array
- The remaining elements of the sequence correspond to the elements of the input array starting from index L onwards
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.
In this case:
    method SplitArrayAtL(a: array<int>, L: int) returns (result: seq<int>)
    
Step 2: Determine the preconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - L should be between 0 and a.Length inclusive, to ensure valid split
    
Dafny specification:
    requires 0 <= L <= a.Length
    
Step 3: Determine the postconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The resulting sequence contains the first L elements of the array
    - The length of the resulting sequence is L
    - The sequence contains precisely the first L elements of the array, in order

Dafny specification:
    ensures result == a[..L]
    ensures |result| == L
    
Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.
In this case:

```dafny
method SplitArrayAtL(a: array<int>, L: int) returns (result: seq<int>)
    requires 0 <= L <= a.Length
    ensures result == a[..L]
    ensures |result| == L
{
    var res: seq<int> := [];
    var i: int := 0;
    while i < L
        invariant 0 <= i <= L
        invariant res == a[..i]
        decreases L - i
    {
        res := res + [a[i]];
        i := i + 1;
    }
    result := res;
}
```
